identity.title: VERTICO. III. The Kennicutt-Schmidt relation in Virgo cluster galaxies

paper_type_evidence.quote: We use new Atacama Compact Array and Total Power (ACA+TP) observations from the VERTICO-ALMA (Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array) Large Program at $720\,\mathrm{pc}$ resolution to resolve the molecular gas content, as traced by the $^{12}\mathrm{CO}\,(2-1)$ transition, across the disks of 37 spiral galaxies in the Virgo cluster.
The observations for VERTICO were carried out using the ALMA Atacama Compact Array (ACA) during Cycle 7 (2019.1.00763.L.).

method.value: Convolve imaged ALMA datacubes to 9" (720 pc) and 15" (1.2 kpc) resolution, apply a spatially and spectrally varying S/N mask (core mask S/N >= 3.5 in >= 3 channels, wing mask S/N >= 2 in >= 2 channels), and integrate along the spectral axis to obtain Moment-0 maps in K km s^-1.

evidence.quote: After imaging, two working datasets were generated by convolving each datacube to 9” resolution and 15” resolution, which correspond to physical scales of 720 pc and 1.2 kpc respectively, at the distance of Virgo.

Moment-$0$ maps are then calculated the integrated intensity along the spectral axis in K km s$^{-1}$.

analysis_steps.goal: Derive molecular gas mass surface density maps

method.value: Convert CO(2-1) integrated intensity maps to molecular gas surface density using Sigma_mol = alpha_CO * (I_CO(2-1) / R_21) * cos(i) for both VERTICO and HERACLES samples.

evidence.quote: In this paper, we derive the molecular surface densities directly from the VERTICO and HERACLES surveys CO (2-1) integrated intensity maps, assuming a fixed CO (2-1)-to-CO (1-0) line ratio, $R_{21}$, of 0.7 as derived by (cite: Brown2021).

key_parameters.value: Inclination cut i <= 80 deg for the 37-galaxy subsample

evidence.quote: Our selected sub-sample only excludes highly-inclined ($i > 80^\mathrm{o}$) targets from the original dataset, in order to minimize any major projection effects.

In this paper, we derive the molecular surface densities directly from the VERTICO and HERACLES surveys CO (2-1) integrated intensity maps, assuming a fixed CO (2-1)-to-CO (1-0) line ratio, $R_{21}$, of 0.7 as derived by (cite: Brown2021).

assumptions.value: Constant Galactic conversion factor alpha_CO = 4.35 M_sun pc^-2 (K km s^-1)^-1 (including 1.36 helium factor)

evidence.quote: Throughout the paper we assume a constant Galactic value, $\alpha^{MW}_{\textrm{CO}}=4.35\,M_\odot\,\textrm{pc}^{-2}\textrm{(K km s}^{-1}\textrm{)}^{-1}$ (cite: Bolatto2013), for which the corresponding $X_\mathrm{CO}$ is $2\times10^{20}\,\textrm{cm}^{-2}\textrm{(K km s}^{-1}\textrm{)}^{-1}$.
This value already includes a 1.36 factor to account for the presence of helium.

analysis_steps.goal: Construct spatially resolved Star Formation Rate (SFR) surface density maps

method.value: Mask Gaia DR2 stars, subtract background using Astropy Background2D, convolve GALEX NUV and WISE images to 9" using Aniano et al. (2011) kernels, apply a pixel-by-pixel radial linear WISE3-to-WISE4 color correction to WISE3 images, and apply the Leroy et al. (2019) NUV+WISE4 SFR calibration.

evidence.quote: All images are convolved from their native resolution to a common working resolution of 9", using the (cite: Aniano2011) convolution kernels. All Gaia Data Release (DR) 2 stars within the image area were masked. Image backgrounds are estimated and subtracted with the Astropy Background2D function.

Specifically, for each galaxy we fit a linear relation between WISE3/WISE4 color and galactocentric radius and then modify the WISE3 image on a pixel-by-pixel basis according to the galactocentric radius of each pixel and the expected WISE3/WISE4 ratio from the linear fit.

With GALEX NUV and color-corrected WISE3 images for each galaxy, we then apply the NUV+WISE4 SFR calibration from (cite: Leroy2019) to derive spatially resolved SFR maps in units $M_\odot$/yr/kpc$^2$.

claims.hypothesis: The ensemble resolved Kennicutt-Schmidt relation in Virgo cluster spiral galaxies operates similarly to that of isolated field galaxies.
claims.experiment: Measured Sigma_mol from VERTICO ALMA ACA+TP CO(2-1) maps and Sigma_SFR from GALEX NUV + WISE3 photometry at 720 pc resolution across 37 Virgo spiral galaxies, fitted the ensemble KS relation using Least Trimmed Squares regression, and compared with 21 HERACLES field galaxies.
claims.result: Derived an ensemble KS slope of N = 0.97 +/- 0.07, scatter of 0.42 dex, and characteristic depletion time of 1.86 Gyr, closely matching HERACLES field galaxies.
claims.finding: To first order, when considered as an ensemble, star formation in Virgo cluster disk galaxies operates in a similar way to isolated star-forming galaxies.

evidence.quote: We find the KS slope for the entire population to be $N=0.97\pm0.07$, with a characteristic molecular gas depletion time of $1.86\,\mathrm{Gyr}$ for our full sample, in agreement with previous work in isolated, nearby star-forming galaxies.

evidence.loc: Ensemble Star Formation Relations in VERTICO
evidence.quote: Figure [2](#fig:global-ks-inc) therefore demonstrates visually the first main conclusion of this paper: when considered as an ensemble, the KS relation for Virgo cluster disk galaxies is consistent with field galaxies.

claims.hypothesis: The resolved Kennicutt-Schmidt parameters depend on spatial scale between 720 pc and 1.2 kpc.
claims.experiment: Convolved the VERTICO and ancillary datasets to 15" (1.2 kpc) resolution and repeated the Least Trimmed Squares fit to the ensemble KS relation.
claims.result: At 1.2 kpc scales, the KS slope is N = 0.91 +/- 0.08 (or +/- 0.09 in text) with a scatter of 0.35 dex, consistent within uncertainties with the 720 pc result (N = 0.97 +/- 0.07).
claims.finding: There are no significant differences in the resolved KS parameters between 720 pc and 1.2 kpc resolutions.

evidence.loc: Ensemble Star Formation Relations in VERTICO
evidence.quote: We perform the same robust fit to the data shown in the right panel of Figure [2](#fig:global-ks-inc), and derive a slope of $0.91 \pm 0.09$ with a RMS scatter of $\Sigma_\mathrm{SFR}$ about the fit of 0.35 dex, at 1.2 kpc scales.

evidence.loc: Ensemble Star Formation Relations in VERTICO
evidence.quote: These results indicate that there are no significant differences in the KS parameters as a consequence of working at different resolutions, these agree well within the uncertainties of the data.

claims.hypothesis: Cluster environmental processes (traced by HI-deficiency) modify the resolved KS relation and reduce the star formation efficiency of molecular gas.
claims.experiment: Divided the VERTICO sample into HI-deficient (def_HI,M* > 0.3) and HI-normal subsamples, fitted their resolved KS relations, compared their positions on the SFR-M* plane, and computed Pearson correlations between HI-deficiency and M*, SFR, and sSFR.
claims.result: HI-deficient galaxies have a steeper KS slope (N = 0.93 +/- 0.04) and lower mean SFE (<log10 Sigma_SFR/Sigma_mol> = -9.34 +/- 0.04) than HI-normal galaxies (N = 0.84 +/- 0.04, <log10 Sigma_SFR/Sigma_mol> = -9.10 +/- 0.06), and lie on average 0.60 dex below the SFMS at fixed stellar mass.
claims.finding: Environmental mechanisms affecting HI content directly reduce the star formation efficiency of molecular gas in cluster galaxies, leading to longer depletion times and systematic quenching.

evidence.loc: The KS relation in HI-deficient environments
evidence.quote: By using the same fitting methodology described in Section [5.1](#sec:ensemble), we obtain a resolved KS slope of $N=0.93\pm0.04$, a $< \mathrm{log}_{10} \Sigma_\mathrm{SFR}/\Sigma_\mathrm{mol} > =-9.34\pm0.04$ and a 1-$\sigma$ scatter of 0.30 dex for those galaxies classified as HI-deficient.

evidence.loc: The KS relation in HI-deficient environments
evidence.quote: In comparison, the resulting quantities for the HI-normal galaxies show a characteristic slope of $N=0.84\pm0.04$, a $< \mathrm{log}_{10} \Sigma_\mathrm{SFR}/\Sigma_\mathrm{mol} > =-9.10\pm0.06$ and a 1-$\sigma$ scatter of 0.41 dex.

This implies that the environmental mechanisms affecting the HI galaxy content also have a direct impact in the local molecular gas content and its star formation efficiency, which are reduced in HI-deficient cluster galaxies.

claims.hypothesis: A single universal resolved Kennicutt-Schmidt relation describes individual cluster disk galaxies.
claims.experiment: Performed individual Least Trimmed Squares fits to the 720 pc resolved KS relation for each of the 37 VERTICO galaxies.
claims.result: Individual galaxy KS slopes range from 0.69 to 1.40 (with 2 galaxies unable to be fit by a power law), individual scatter averages +/- 0.21 dex, and typical molecular gas star formation efficiencies vary by a factor of ~4, accounting for ~0.20 dex of the 0.42 dex ensemble scatter.
claims.finding: There is significant galaxy-to-galaxy and sub-galactic variation in KS relations, confirming that no single resolved KS relation accurately describes every galaxy.

evidence.loc: The KS relation for individual galaxies
evidence.quote: Table [\[tab:indiv_slopes\]](#tab:indiv_slopes) shows that the slopes obtained by fitting individual $\Sigma_\textrm{SFR}$-to-$\Sigma_\textrm{mol}$ relations range between $N=0.69$ and $N=1.40$, with a mean typical scatter of $\pm0.21$dex.

evidence.loc: The KS relation for individual galaxies
evidence.quote: When visually inspecting the panels, it is clear that there is significant galaxy-to-galaxy variation (take galaxies NGC 4457 and NGC 4713 as examples), confirming that there is no single resolved KS relation that can accurately describe every galaxy.

claims.hypothesis: External gravitational and hydrodynamic cluster interactions create azimuthal variations in resolved molecular gas star formation efficiency across galaxy disks.
claims.experiment: Sampled each galaxy with 18 radial vectors from its optical center and examined the resolved SFE and KS relation as a function of azimuthal angular separation from a reference interaction direction.
claims.result: Strong azimuthal variations were found in NGC 4654 (depletion time ~0.9 Gyr within ~70 deg of interaction direction with NGC 4639 vs ~0.5 Gyr on the opposite side) and NGC 4383 (median depletion time ~0.4 Gyr along the semi-minor axis vs longer depletion times at ~80-120 deg).
claims.finding: Tidal interactions and ram-pressure stripping directly affect the resolved physical properties and star formation efficiency of molecular gas within cluster galaxy disks.

evidence.quote: Figure [7](#fig:angle_az) shows that disk regions within $\sim 70^o$ from the direction of interaction tend to follow a KS relation characterized by slightly longer depletion times ($\sim0.9$ Gyr) than those regions in the opposite side ($\sim0.5$ Gyr).

We observe clear azimuthal variations of the molecular gas depletion times in two of our galaxies, NGC 4383 and NGC 4654. These can be directly linked to the presence of gravitational tidal interactions and ram-pressure stripping of the gas, respectively, and provide additional evidence that the cluster environment directly affects the resolved physical properties of the molecular gas.

why_this_data.value: VERTICO provides homogeneous sub-kpc (720 pc) CO(2-1) mapping across a statistically significant sample of 51 Virgo cluster galaxies actively affected by ram pressure stripping, starvation, and tidal interactions, while excluding i > 80 deg minimizes projection and extinction effects.

evidence.quote: While recent efforts have been made in this direction, VERTICO is the first survey probing the molecular gas content at sub-kpc scales in a complete and statistically significant number of galaxies of the Virgo cluster.
Our selected sub-sample only excludes highly-inclined ($i > 80^\mathrm{o}$) targets from the original dataset, in order to minimize any major projection effects.

why_this_method.value: Least Trimmed Squares (LTS) regression accounts for uncertainties in both variables, outliers, and intrinsic scatter; WISE3 is used with a radial WISE3/WISE4 color correction because WISE3 reaches 9" resolution matching ALMA while WISE4 is a more robust SFR tracer.

evidence.quote: We use WISE3 images to quantify the obscured SFR at an angular resolution of 9” similar to the one reached by ALMA.

That said, (cite: Leroy2019) show that WISE4 is a much more robust SFR tracer than WISE3, despite the higher sensitivity and resolution of WISE3 imaging. To address this we apply a pixel-by-pixel WISE3-to-WISE4 color correction to the WISE3 images.

evidence.loc: Ensemble Star Formation Relations in VERTICO
evidence.quote: In order to better quantify this relation, we perform a robust linear regression following the method presented in (cite: Cappellari2013), which implements the least trimmed squares (LTS) regression approach of (cite: Rousseeuw1984). This method takes into account the uncertainties in all variables, the presence of outliers in the data, as well as unknown intrinsic scatter in excess of uncertainties.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Using a metallicity-dependent CO-to-H2 conversion factor instead of a constant Galactic alpha_CO = 4.35

evidence.quote: It is well known that the CO-to-H$_2$ conversion factor depends on metallicity (cite: Wilson1995; Boselli2002; Bolatto2013; Sandstrom2013). The galaxies analyzed in this work are all massive spirals with a similar metallicity range. We thus decided to use a similar conversion factor for all of them.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Using WISE4 (22 um) directly instead of color-corrected WISE3 (12 um) for obscured SFR tracing

evidence.quote: The WISE3 band is preferred to the WISE4 band at $22\mu$m for its better angular resolution, although the latter is believed to be a better SFR tracer due to less contamination from polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAH) emission (cite: Boselli2004).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Using Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) or bisector regressions instead of Least Trimmed Squares (LTS)

evidence.quote: It is worth noting that interpreting the results from simple bisector and OLS regressions is statistically hard, since a linear slope could even result from a scenario where there is no correlation between a predictor and its response (cite: Isobe1990; Shetty2014).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Weighting each line-of-sight measurement by the inverse number of measurements per galaxy in the ensemble fit

evidence.quote: We address this issue by weighting each line-of-sight measurement by the number of independent measurements that a given galaxy contributes to the overall sample, as also described in (cite: Zabel2020).

limitations_admitted.value: Fitted parameter uncertainties do not include systematic uncertainties from the choice of SFR tracer or variations in the alpha_CO conversion factor (which varies with metallicity, SFR surface density, and in galaxy centers/outflows).

While we have adopted a constant value in this work, it is well known that the CO-to-H$_2$ conversion factor varies within and among galaxies.

In the presence of an AGN, the SFR derived using a combination of UV and IR tracers is likely inaccurate.

referee_caveats_inferred: Non-detections / upper limits in CO(2-1) are excluded by the S/N masking prior to fitting, which can censor low-Sigma_mol data and bias the fitted KS slope toward flatter/sub-linear values.
The azimuthal SFE split in Section 5.4 is chosen 'by eye' to maximize visual divergence in the KS diagram without a quantitative statistical significance test across all 37 galaxies.
Assuming a constant R_21 = 0.7 and constant alpha_CO = 4.35 across both ram-pressure-stripped outer disks and galaxy centers may systematically skew radial and environmental trends in Sigma_mol.
